newsitem.title: UK: Guinness, Grand Met chiefs to meet LVMH head.
newsitem.headline: Guinness, Grand Met chiefs to meet LVMH head.

text.p: The heads of Guinness PLC and Grand Metropolitan PLC will go to Paris to meet LVMH chairman Bernard Arnault on Wednesday in an effort to open the way to a merger of the three companies, a source close to Guinness said on Sunday.
"There is only one issue on the table," the source said.

Tony Greener and George Bull, chairmen respectively of Guinness and Grand Met, will travel to Paris to try and break the deadlock which has seen LVMH trying to block a merger between Guinness and Grand Met.

The Saturday edition of The Daily Telegraph said Greener and Bull might suggest that Arnault's Moet Hennessey be injected into UDV, the new spirits company which is being created from merging Grand Met's IDV and Guinness's United Distillers.
In return, Arnault would own an equity stake in IDV. Bringing Moet Hennessey into UDV could generate up to 85 million stg additional cost savings, the paper said.
LVMH has been buying Grand Met shares to block the proposed merger between Grand Met and Guinness in which it holds 14.2 percent.

So far it has acquired around 6.37 percent of the capital of Grand Met, spending 8.5 billion francs. LVMH is believed to be planning to keep buying Grand Met stock until it has acquired at least 10 percent at which point it could call an extraordinary shareholders' meeting.
Analysts expect LVMH chairman Bernard Arnault to try to win enough allies in Grand Met to build up a 25 percent block to prevent the merger from going ahead.
His goal is to create a powerful drinks group combining all their brands.
